questions.stem: A patient presented with seizures, muscle tremors, backward arching of the spine after consuming some herbal medicine. What is the most likely cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Strychnine poisoning

Strychnine poisoning can be fatal to humans and other animals and can occur by inhalation, swallowing or absorption through eyes or mouth. It produces some of the most dramatic and painful symptoms of any known toxic reaction, making it quite noticeable and a common choice for assassinations .



THE ESSENTIALS OF FORENSIC MEDICINE AND TOXICOLOGY 33RD EDITION PAGE NO. 612,613,155,554,616,563

questions.stemHtml: Identify the given histological image ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glomeruli

The image shows three histological structures: the capillary endothelium of the glomeruli, specialized cells called podocytes, and the fused basement membranes of both of these cells

questions.stem: A 45-year-old chronic alcoholic presents with abdominal pain. Laboratory tests reveal an alkaline phosphatase (ALP) level of 230 U/L and a conjugated bilirubin (BB) level of 1 mg/dL. In addition, the alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is found to be significantly elevated. What is the most likely diagnosis for this patient's clinical presentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hepatocellular carcinoma

  • The given clinical scenario suggests the diagnosis of HCC- Hepatocellular carcinoma.
  • It is a primary malignant tumor of the liver. It commonly occurs in individuals with risk factors such as chronic alcoholism and liver cirrhosis. In this case, the patient's chronic alcoholism history and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) level strongly suggest the possibility of HCC.



Robbins Basic pathology, 10th edition, Page no 432, 434

questions.stem: An Infant presented with progressive jaundice and pale colored stool. The liver biopsy showed bile plugs, bile duct proliferation and polymorphonuclear infiltrate. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Extra hepatic biliary atresia
  • Based on the clinical presentation and the liver biopsy findings described, the most likely diagnosis for the infant would be extrahepatic biliary atresia.
  • It  is a condition in which there is complete or partial obstruction or absence of the bile ducts outside the liver. It is a rare condition that usually presents in infancy and is characterized by progressive jaundice, pale-colored stools, and hepatomegaly .


Nelson textbook of pediatrics 21st edition Page no: 2098-2099,2102,2103

questions.stem: A 64 year old male went for a medical checkup and accidently found an increased WBC count of 95000 / Cubic mm. Lab investigations showed a marked elevation of lymphocytes with marked leukocytosis. What will be your next investigation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flow cytometry

The likely diagnosis based on the given clinical scenario and the peripheral smear showing smudge cells is chronic lymphocytic leukemia. The next step in his management should be flow cytometry.



ROBBINS AND COTRAN PATHOLOGIC BASIS OF DISEASE 10TH EDITION 597-599
